title: Trip Settlement and Point Calculation
how_it_works_companion: How It Works chapter 10, section HOW POINT CALCULATIONS WORK

sections.business_context:
Settlement is where a trip becomes a number. The member is charged for the days they had the car
and the miles they drove beyond their allowance, and that charge posts to their points ledger.
This guide covers the calculation: what is counted, from which snapshot, in what order, and how the
result is recorded so that it can be explained years later.
The rule that governs it, and the one just settled: a trip settles once, at its end, and its cost never
changes. Credits, including a free-pass weekend, post separately against the member rather than
reducing the trip. Nothing is ever repriced.
Pairs with How It Works chapter 10, section HOW POINT CALCULATIONS WORK.
sections.schema_overview:
WHAT SETTLEMENT READS AND WRITES

Column                           Purpose

weekday_count_actual,
                                 How many of each the trip actually was.
weekend_count_actual

vehicle_tier_snapshot            The tier at checkout.

weekday_point_value_snapshot,
                                 What each cost, frozen at checkout.
weekend_point_value_snapshot

extra_mile_point_value_snapshot What an extra mile cost, frozen at checkout.

included_miles_snapshot          The allowance for this trip, computed at checkout.

overage_miles_snapshot           Miles beyond the allowance.

base_points                      Days times their rates.

extra_mileage_points             Overage times the extra-mile rate.

total_points                     What the trip cost. Final.

credits_applied_points           Credits recorded against the trip for reference. See below.

calculation_version,
                                 Which rules produced this, and the working.
calculation_detail
sections.implementation_workflow:
1) Counting the Days
    1. Count weekdays and weekends from the actual trip, not the reservation.
    2. A weekend is one unit covering Friday afternoon to Monday morning, priced as a single
       bundled figure. It is never three weekdays.
    3. A member returning early on Sunday still had the weekend. The bundled rate applies in full.


    4. A trip spanning a weekend and weekdays counts both: the weekend as one unit and the
       weekdays individually.
    5. Store the counts. They are what makes the arithmetic checkable afterwards.

2) Computing the Base Charge
    1. Multiply the weekday count by the weekday snapshot value, and the weekend count by the
       weekend snapshot value. Add them.
    2. Use the snapshots taken at checkout, never the current rate card. This is why the snapshots
       exist.
    3. Store the result as base_points.

3) Computing the Mileage Charge
    1. The allowance is the daily figure times the number of days the member had the car, with a
       weekend counting as three days because mileage is per day even though the price is bundled.
    2. Where a level uses the annual bucket structure instead of a daily allowance, the trip’s miles
       draw against the year’s bucket rather than a per-trip figure. No current level offers it and the
       structure must still be supported. See the Membership Plans chapter.
    3. The allowance was snapshotted at checkout as included_miles_snapshot.
    4. Overage is member miles less the allowance, floored at zero, stored as
       overage_miles_snapshot.
    5. Multiply overage by the extra-mile snapshot value. That value is fractional, so round once at
       the end rather than at each step.
    6. Store the result as extra_mileage_points.

EXAMPLE — A WEEKEND TRIP SETTLING

Step                          Figure           Source

Weekend count                 1                Actual trip

Weekend point value           35               Snapshot at checkout

Base points                   35               1 times 35

Included miles                300              100 per day times 3 weekend days

Member miles                  412              Odometer less club-added miles

Overage miles                 112              412 less 300

Extra-mile value              0.250            Snapshot at checkout

Extra mileage points          28               112 times 0.250

Total points                  63               35 plus 28



4) Posting the Charge
    1. total_points is base_points plus extra_mileage_points. That is what the trip cost.
    2. Post it to the member’s points ledger against the package the trip drew from.
    3. Where the package is split, draw from the participant’s share; where pooled, from the pool.
       See the Member Management chapter.
    4. A balance may go negative. The charge is applied in full regardless.
    5. The trip is now settled and its cost never changes.
    6. Where the vehicle belongs to a vehicle owner program partner, settlement also generates the
       owner’s member-trip mileage payout entry from the same chargeable miles that produced the
       member’s charge. That entry is one lane of the partner’s mileage earnings, not the whole: the
       partner is paid for the club’s use of the car, so operational miles outside member trips earn
       separately, and miles attached to a non-earning service trip do not earn at all (the VOP guide
       owns that rule).
    7. Deriving the owner’s figure separately would let the two disagree, and the disagreement would
       be invisible until a partner questioned a statement. In particular, recomputing from the
       odometer alone would miss any goodwill adjustment the member received.
    8. The payout calculation is specified in the Vehicle Owner Program chapter. What belongs here
       is that settlement is the moment it is created, and that idempotency covers it: a re-submitted
       trip produces no second payout entry.

5) Credits Are Separate
    1. A free-pass weekend does not reduce total_points. It posts as a credit against the member,
       linked to the trip it is applied to, and that link may move to a more valuable trip later.
    2. credits_applied_points records what credit is currently sitting on this trip, for display. It is a
       reference, not a component of the charge.
    3. Any other credit, whether goodwill or promotional, posts the same way: against the member,
       not into the trip.
    4. This is what allows a member to read a statement months later and find every trip figure
       unchanged. See the Reservations chapter for the credit mechanics.

6) Recording the Working
    1. Idempotency. Settlement checks whether it has already posted before writing anything, so re-
       running it is always safe. A settled trip re-submitted must produce no second charge, no
       second payout entry, and no second ledger line.
    2. Test for the existing settlement on the trip itself rather than for the ledger entry alone, because
       a partial failure could leave one written and not the other.
    3. Store calculation_version so the club knows which rules produced this figure, and so a trip
       settled years ago is always understood under the rules that applied then.
    4. Store calculation_detail as a complete trace: the resolved tier, the rates, the day counts, the
       mileage arithmetic, the perks applied, and the totals. Anyone should be able to reconstruct the
       settlement by hand and reach the same number.
    5. Store calculation_detail as the working: the counts, the rates, the allowance, the overage, and
       the arithmetic.
    6. A member questioning a charge should be answerable from the record alone, without anybody
       recomputing anything.
    7. When the calculation rules change, the version changes. Old trips keep their version and their
       figures.
sections.rules_and_constraints:
1. A trip settles once, at its end, and total_points never changes afterwards.
    2. Day counts come from the actual trip, not the reservation - except under a granted courtesy.
       Where the only difference between actual custody and the scheduled window is an early
       pickup or late return granted on the reservation, settlement reads the scheduled window for
       both days and mileage allowance: the member bought Friday to Monday and that is what
       settles, with Thursday’s driving drawing from the allowance they already hold.
    3. Usage reporting reads real custody. A member who drove sixty-three billed days with two early
       pickups genuinely drove sixty-five, and days-driven reporting counts them - a courtesy day is
       identified by a grant on the reservation with the actual checkout date before the scheduled
       start. A late return never adds a day.
    4. A weekend is one bundled unit and is never three weekdays.
    5. An early return still pays the full weekend rate.
    6. Every rate used comes from the checkout snapshot, never the current card.
    7. Mileage allowance counts three days for a weekend.
    8. Settlement is idempotent: it checks for an existing settlement before writing anything.
    9. Every settlement stores its calculation version and a complete trace of its working.
    10. A level on the annual bucket structure draws trip miles against the year rather than a per-trip
        allowance.
    11. Overage is floored at zero.
    12. Rounding happens once, at the end.
    13. Credits post against the member and never reduce the trip figure.
    14. Fuel bills itself: at trip close the platform computes the fuel consumed (fuel_start_percent to
        fuel_end_percent, plus refuel events on the trip) and automatically posts a Fuel member
        charge marked up at membership_level_pricing.fuel_markup_percent. Staff never key this
        charge.
    15. An accepted delivery quote posts itself the same way. Where
        vehicle_reservation.delivery_quote_accepted_at is set, settlement posts a
        MEMBER_CHARGE of type Delivery for vehicle_reservation.delivery_quote_amount, in
        dollars. Post the accepted amount, never a recalculation - the miles and the rate row were
        snapshotted at the quote, and a branch rate changed since then must not move a price the
        member already agreed to. An empty acceptance stamp posts nothing, which is also the
        correct outcome for a delivery the perk covered.
    16. Settlement generates the partner’s member-trip payout entry from the same chargeable miles
        as the member charge (one lane of the partner’s mileage earnings - see the VOP guide for the
        full earning basis).
    17. The calculation version and working are stored with every settled trip.
sections.integration_and_edge_cases:
1. A rate card replaced between checkout and check-in. Irrelevant. The snapshot was taken
       at checkout and settlement uses it.
    2. A weekend trip returned Sunday morning. Full weekend rate, three days of mileage
       allowance. Both follow from the weekend being one unit.



    3. A delivery or collection trip where the staff-driven leg is missing from the member’s total. It
       should not be missing: the showroom-to-showroom rule puts those miles on the member’s tab
       as extra_miles, and a delivery can correctly push a member over their allowance.
    4. A member with no points left. The charge posts and the balance goes negative. Settlement
       does not refuse.
    5. A trip whose free-pass credit later moves away. The trip figure is unchanged; only the
       credit moved. The member’s balance adjusts, not the trip.
    6. A calculation rule changing next year. New version, new trips. Old trips keep their version
       and remain explicable.
    7. A member disputing a charge. The stored working answers it: what was counted, at what
       rate, against what allowance.
    8. A trip on a corporate package. Charged to the company through the package. The
       participant records who drove.
sections.automations_and_notifications:
Each automation below is listed with its trigger and its expected outcome. Operational specification is
reserved for the automations pass that follows the first draft of all chapters.

AUTOMATIONS IN THIS GUIDE

Trigger                         Outcome

Check-in completed              Settlement runs; counts, charges, and working recorded.

Settlement complete             Points posted to the ledger; member notified with the figure.

Overage charged                 Detail shown to the member: allowance, miles driven, and rate.

Free-pass credit placed or
                                Member balance adjusted; no trip figure changes.
moved

Balance going negative          Surfaced to staff.



Reserved for the automations pass: settlement timing after check-in, the content of the member
notification, and whether a large overage is reviewed before posting.
sections.developer_notes:
1. Read the snapshot, never the card. Settlement must not touch a rate card. Every figure it
       needs was frozen at checkout, and reading live would reprice completed trips whenever a card
       changed.
    2. A weekend is one unit for price and three days for mileage. Both halves are
       counterintuitive and both are right. Treating a weekend as three weekdays for price, or one
       day for mileage, are the two most likely bugs in this guide.
    3. Round once. The extra-mile value is fractional. Rounding per mile produces a figure that
       disagrees with the working by a point or two, which is exactly the kind of discrepancy a
       member notices.
    4. Credits are not components. total_points is base plus mileage. A credit posts elsewhere.
       Subtracting it here would reintroduce the repricing problem the credit model exists to remove.


    5. Store the working. It costs a text column and saves every dispute. Recomputing to answer a
       question invites a different answer.
    6. Version the calculation. When the rules change, old trips must keep producing their original
       figures, and the version is how anybody knows which rules applied.
    7. Never refuse on balance. Settlement records what happened. A member without points still
       drove the car.
